messages.text: Quick question on fee schedule exceptions. {{CLIENT_NAME:c_0268}} is asking us to hold the 0.85% advisory rate on {{ACCOUNT_NUMBER:a_00552}} after the AUM bump. Anyone know who signs off on that now? Tricia is out today.
Anything below the standard tier breakpoint needs Grace's approval plus a note in ClientHub. Tricia can't approve her own exception as the RM either.
Got it. Is there a form or is it just a ClientHub note?
There's a Fee Exception Request template in the shared drive under Wealth > Forms. Needs the rationale, the proposed rate, and the expiry date. I can pre-fill it if you give me the details.

Related: I have a similar one. {{CLIENT_NAME:c_0039}} wants the cash management sleeve ({{ACCOUNT_NUMBER:a_00084}}) billed at the same rate as the brokerage side ({{ACCOUNT_NUMBER:a_00083}}). Is that a real exception or just householding?
Householding if both accounts are linked in PortfolioMgr under one billing group. If they're not linked, the blended tier won't apply and it becomes an exception. Check the billing group field first.
Just checked. They're not linked. I'll ask David whether there was a reason, otherwise I'll request the link rather than an exception.
Good call. Linking is cleaner and doesn't leave a permanent exception on the books. Auditors always ask about those.
James, yes please. Proposed rate 0.85%, 12 month expiry, rationale: household assets crossed the next tier after the recent contribution, client is also consolidating an outside account with us.
Drafted and saved to the drive. Linked it in ClientHub on the client record. Still needs Tricia's rationale confirmation before it goes to Grace.
Reminder for everyone: if the client emails or calls about fees, log it in ClientHub the same day. {{CLIENT_EMAIL:c_0268}} came up in an old thread and the contact history was missing.
Fair point, I'll log my call notes now. Will also ping Tricia Monday morning so the request isn't sitting over the weekend.
Sounds good. If Grace hasn't approved by Wednesday, flag it here and we'll chase her. The client's next billing run is the 1st, so we have time but not much.
